description: JSON parsing/serialization and the fetch API.

questions.question: What does JSON.parse do and when does it throw?
questions.answer:
JSON.parse converts a JSON string into a JavaScript value. It throws a SyntaxError when the input is not valid JSON, including trailing commas or single quotes.

code:
const user = JSON.parse('{"name": "Ana"}');
console.log(user.name);  // Ana

real example:
Parsing a response body validates the server returned real JSON; a broken payload produces a SyntaxError you can catch and assert on.
